$comment: Academy family (docs/map-briefs/st_johns, step 1): a dormitory floor in bays, for halls of any length on one, two or three floors. A hall is a row of Dorm Bays (1 × 2 cells: the hall down the middle, two rooms each side) between two Stair End Bays, with the Dorm Office Bay in the middle. All run west to east in their own frame, the hall's middle on the line between the two rows of cells (4 m north of the anchor cell's centre), 2.4 m wide at every bay's ends. Parts as in carriageway.json; parts are only ever added at the end. Edit, then run `node tools/content/setpieces.mjs`.

pieces.blurb: 8 m of a dormitory floor, 1 × 2 cells: a hall down the middle, two rooms each side, each with an oak door between two built-in closets, a sink, two desks with hutches, a bunk and a sash window. Place bays end to end.

choices.blurb: The oak door fills the room's 2 m doorway, as first built.

choices.label: Slim (1.2 m)
choices.blurb: The doorway brought in by a jamb either side, a 1.2 m oak door in it (bots walk through on a link: sim/passages.ts).

choices.label: Paired (lighter)

notes.design: Two Rooms open to each other and at both ends; the hall straddles the line between them (z 2.8 to 5.2 m from the anchor cell's centre). Its walls are blocks 0.72 m thick, a closet deep: three piers a side to the doors' heads (2.6 m) and one beam over them, so each room's 2 m doorway is a reveal 0.6 m deep between two built-in closets (2 m: bots keep 0.8 m off walls). The closets are the wall: a Built-in Closet Front (a still prop, 12 mm proud, no collision) in its face either side of the doorway. A partition 0.12 m thick between the two rooms of a side, and half a partition at each end, so two bays side by side make a whole one. Rooms are 3.88 m wide and 6.18 m from the hall wall to the window (5.58 m past the closets). Each: an Oak Door standing open in the reveal (a still prop, no collision), a sink unit on the left 0.9 m past the closet's front (the closet door has room), two desks with hutches along the left wall (the second by the window), a chair pushed in at each (not solid), a bunk on the right by the window (Twin sash windows, one a room). Clear floor: 2.08 m between the desks and the bunk, 1.93 m between a chair's back and the bunk. One light, in the hall. A room's pieces are in one order for the four rooms, so a placement can hide a room's furniture by part index.

pieces.blurb: A Dorm Bay with the two north rooms shut: one door closed, one ajar, bulletproof glass in their windows. Half the rooms of a floor to duck into, half not.

notes.design: The Dorm Bay with its north rooms closed: an Oak Door shut and one ajar (both collide as the doorway's slab), the rooms seen through their windows (the bunk, the two desks and the closets' fronts; no chairs, no sink) behind reinforced glass, so nobody climbs in. Turn a bay half round to shut the other side.

pieces.blurb: The end of a two-floor hall, 1 × 2 cells: a half-turn stairwell south, a lobby with the outside door north, the hall's mouth east on both floors.

notes.design: A Stairwell turned so its foot and its upper landing open north onto the lobby (no wall between them), the lobby a Room with a Room doorway west and an Oak Door standing open in it. The east side is closed by walls of its own but for the hall's mouth (z 2.8 to 5.2 m), which a Dorm Bay's hall meets on both floors. The Stairwell's upper landing leaves a corner open; a floor block closes it and a rail stands over the flight. The stairwell wears the hall's facade (plinth, buttresses, battlements) as the rooms do: a facade is the one room option a piece may give a tile that is not a Room (map/setPieceCheck.ts); its inner walls are in the stone role, its steps in the trim's, and a plaster ceiling under a roof block closes its top (stairs take no ceiling option). Turn it half round for a hall's other end.

pieces.blurb: The end of a three-floor hall, 1 × 2 cells: half-turn stairwells, the first south, the second north over the lobby, a landing room at the top; the hall's mouth east on every floor.

notes.design: As the Stair End Bay, a floor taller: a Stairwell takes two levels of its cell, so the second one stands in the other cell (over the lobby), turned to open south onto the first one's upper landing; the top floor's landing room is over the first. Floor blocks close the landings' open corners (the second at the hall's mouth), rails stand over the flights.

notes.design: A straight Stairs tile fills its cell (a 7 m flight, 8 m long) and takes two levels, with its foot in the cell west of it and its head in the cell east: so the bay is three cells long and two floors high, and the hall beside the stair runs north of the cells' line (z 4 to 6.4 m), 3.6 m wide at the two ends where it meets a Dorm Bay's hall (z 2.8 to 5.2 m). North of the hall on each floor: a bathroom (toilets in stalls, basins), the office (an Oak Door with a glazed leaf standing open, a desk, bookcases) directly across from the stair, a bathroom (showers, basins). South: the stair hall at the foot (ground floor, west) and at the head (upstairs, east); the officer's quarters behind a shut diamond-panelled Oak Door under the stair's head on the ground floor and over its foot upstairs, seen through reinforced glass. A third floor goes over it as Dorm Bays, reached by the end stairs (a second straight flight cannot stand over the first: a Stairs tile claims both levels of its cell).

notes.design: The hall of a Dorm Bay (2.4 m wide, z 2.8 to 5.2 m, its walls a closet deep) comes in at the west and turns south at x 2.8 to 5.2 m, so the south mouth meets a Dorm Bay turned a quarter (anchored on this piece's anchor cell): the long arm of an L. North of the west leg, the Dorm Bay's two north rooms as they are; east of the south leg, one room (a north room turned a quarter); in the outer corner a lounge (a sofa and two armchairs on a round rug, a fireplace between the windows, a wide cabinet), entered by an Oak Door standing open on the south leg; in the inner corner a washroom (two toilets in stalls, two showers, three basins) through a doorway on the west leg. The inner corner's west and south sides and the north rooms' west end are half partitions, so the bays beside it close them. Two lights: the hall's turn and the lounge.

notes.design: A side entry for a hall's long side (photo 16 of the brief): the south half of a Dorm Bay is an entrance hall, 8 m across, under a Round arch (3.2 m, voussoirs on both faces) in the outer wall, its walls the look's stone inside and out (an arch has no facade to clad it), open to the hall through a 6 m opening between two short piers (the hall's wall is a closet deep, as in a Dorm Bay); benches either side, a rug, two plants. North of the hall, the Dorm Bay's two rooms as they are. Half partitions at its ends, as a Dorm Bay's. Turn it half round for an entry on the other side; a Dorm Bay goes over it on the floor above.

pieces.blurb: A Stair End Bay whose outside door is a round stone arch: the far end of a two-floor hall.

notes.design: The Stair End Bay with a Round arch (3.2 m, voussoirs and a keystone on both faces) for the lobby's outside door instead of a Room doorway, and no door leaf in it; the lobby's walls are the look's stone inside and out (an arch has no facade to clad it). Everything else as the Stair End Bay.

pieces.blurb: A Stair End Bay with a second outside door on the upper floor, over the lobby's: where a bridge or a walkway meets the hall's end.

notes.design: The Stair End Bay with a Room doorway (an Oak Door standing open in it) in the upper landing room's outer wall, over the lobby's door, in place of its sash window: a skybridge or walkway on the first floor comes in there. Everything else as the Stair End Bay.

pieces.blurb: A slim square stone tower to stand against a hall's corner, 5.4 m across and 13 m to its battlements: firing slits up three faces, a small round-headed door at its foot, a ladder inside to a lookout on top.

notes.design: A tower of blocks in the cell's south-east corner (x -1.5 to 3.9, z -3.82 to 1.58 m), so it stands flush against a hall on the cell's east side and flush with that hall's south front: walls 0.5 m thick of the look's stone, a dressed plinth, string courses at each floor, a cornice under a parapet with merlons at the corners and the middle of each side, to 13.75 m. A door 2 m wide (bots keep 0.8 m off walls) under a stepped round head to 2.85 m, dressed with jambs, ring stones and a keystone, opens into a room 4.4 m square; a ladder in it climbs 11.8 m through a hatch to the lookout behind the parapet (the deck is behind the ladder, where a ladder's top lands). Two firing slits 0.22 m wide, one over the other, in the south, west and north faces of the shaft (the east face stands against the hall). Its east face stops 0.1 m short of the cell's edge so it does not share a face with the hall's wall.

notes.design: Scott Johnston / Hazelwood's centre (docs/map-briefs/st_johns, PLAN_2026-11-12.md 3.2, step 3): two cells of hall on three floors with the block in front of them. North of the hall on each floor the Dorm Bay's two rooms a cell (doors wide or slim, the Room doors option); south of it an open landing the width of both cells, through a 6 m opening between short piers on each cell (as the Dorm Entry Bay's). The forward block (the cells a cell south): a half-turn Stairwell west from the ground to the first floor, the entrance hall east under a Round arch (benches, plants), a second Stairwell over the entrance hall from the first floor to the second (a Stairwell takes two levels of its cell, so they alternate cells, as in the Stair End Bay (3 floors)), and a room over the first with twin sashes south. Every stair opens north onto the landings. The forward block wears the hall's facade on its three outer sides, its top floor a twin sash and an arched window. Ends: half partitions at the landings' ends, so the Dorm Bays beside it close them; the hall's mouths meet theirs on every floor. Turrets: a Round Corner Turret in the cell either side of the forward block.

pieces.blurb: A round stone turret 3 m across to stand against a hall's corner, 14 m to its cornice, with merlons, a slate cone or a red shingle cone on top.

notes.design: A solid round turret of blocks in the cell's south-east corner (its centre 1.75 m in from the cell's east and south edges, so its cone's eaves stay in the cell: it stands 0.25 m off a hall on the cell's east side, over the facade's corner buttress, and 0.25 m behind that hall's south front): twelve wall faces of the look's stone 0.5 m thick, a dressed cornice at 14 m and a cap over the hollow inside: 25 blocks and its top, kept few because a map as played holds at most 4,096 entities (St. John's is near it). Top (an option): merlons on every other face of the cornice, or the Conical Turret Roof (kit.roof.cone) in slate or red shingle. Nobody gets in: it is a landmark and cover.

pieces.blurb: 8 m of a school floor, 1 × 2 cells: a hall down the middle, a classroom each side with a wall of sash windows, twelve desks facing a chalkboard and a screen, the teacher's desk. Place bays end to end.

choices.label: Open (the hall goes on)
choices.blurb: The hall and the rooms run on into the next bay east, as every bay but the last.

choices.label: Closed (the hall's end)
choices.blurb: An outer wall across the east end: the last bay of a floor that ends here (the top floor over a lower end bay).

notes.design: Two Rooms open to each other and at both ends; the hall straddles the line between them (z 2.8 to 5.2 m from the anchor cell's centre) between plastered walls 0.3 m thick, each with a 2 m doorway at the back of its classroom (x 1.3 to 3.3: bots keep 0.8 m off walls) and an Oak Door standing open in it. A half partition at each end, so two bays side by side make a whole one. Each classroom is 7.9 m long and 6 m from the hall wall to the windows (Classroom windows: four sashes). It faces west: a Chalkboard hung 0.85 m up on the west partition with a Projector Screen above it, the teacher's Desk before it, then three School Desks rows (four desks and their chairs each, one prop a row, two each side of an aisle), from the windows to 0.3 m short of the hall's side; the aisle along the hall wall (2.3 m) and the back (2.6 m) are clear for bots. One light, in the hall. East end Closed swaps the east side's open edges for an outer wall and stops the hall's walls at it (the top floor over a lower end bay). Props a bay: 14.
